predecessors.name: Babylonia
predecessors.text: the far south of Mesopotamia, lost to "a native Akkadian-speaking king Ilum-ma-ili" (Babylonia page)

successors.name: Babylonia
successors.text: the Sealand, which Ulam-Buriash "conquered ... incorporated into Babylonia"

capitals.name: Dur-Enlil (site unknown; Lagash, Nippur and Tell Dehaila are proposed)

ledger.x: c. 1732 BC: Ilum-ma-ili founds the Sealand dynasty in the far south. The page dates it "very speculatively c. 1732-1475 BC (MC)" and names Ilum-ma-ilī "the founder of the dynasty" without a founding year; Samsu-iluna's page places the revolt in his years 18-29 (1732-1721), after the pretender Rim-Sin II (year 9)…

c. 1460 BC: the Kassites conquer the Sealand. "The fall of the First Sealand dynasty in 1460 BC created a power vacuum which the Kassites filled"; Ulam-Buriash, brother of Kashtiliash III, "conquered the Sealand, incorporated it into Babylonia" (Sealand page), Ea-gamil "fled to Elam"; Agum III then attacked it again…

wars.name: Ilum-ma-ili's revolt
wars.outcome: Ilum-ma-ili "attacked and brought about the defeat of (Samsu-iluna's) army" (Sealand page) and Nippur "recognized Ilum-ma-ili as king" by Samsu-iluna's death (Samsu-iluna page); Abi-ešuḫ "set out to conquer Ilum-ma-ilī" without result.

wars.name: Kassite conquest of the Sealand
wars.outcome: Ulam-Buriash conquered the Sealand and incorporated it into Babylonia; Agum III attacked it and destroyed a temple in Dur-Enlil.

certainty.note: The dynasty's extent is not on any page: the corrected shape is a reading of "Sumer", with the marshes and the Gulf head as the sure core.
